messages:
incident-bot: PAGED: PagerDuty alert fired for service=redwood-inference-dedicated-us-east-1 — elevated 5xx rate and inference timeouts, triggered by anomaly-detector. PD incident: PDR-39284. Auto-escalation window started.

alex kim: Acked in PD, i'm on it. jumping onto the bridge now. linking logs and initial heap of errors.

maya ramos: thanks alex — i'm on standby to take handoff if you need a swap. any immediate mitigation steps? what customers are impacted?

alex kim: quick summary — intermittent 502/504 and connection reset on model-serving nodes. spike started ~10m ago, peaked at ~18% 5xx across routing tier. Affects hosted text-gen routes and some dedicated pools. customer-facing errors for long requests (>8s).

jordan li: added bridge and runbook links: https://meet.redwood/bridge/PDR-39284 and https://confluence.redwood/ops/runbooks/inference-dedicated-failures. runbook suggests quick check of kvcache evictions + autoscaler flapping.

alex kim: logs snippet:```ERROR: /serve/infer - rpc error: code=13 desc="transport is closing"
trace id=tx-9f3c: conn reset by peer
worker-17: oom-kill? no, kubeevict: pod restarted 3x```

sarah nguyen: ops note — EU dedicated pool has spare capacity, we can route a small percentage to eu-west for immediate relief while we stabilize US pool. will coordinate with infra to ensure data residency flags are OK for in-flight requests.

alex kim: executing traffic split to eu-west (10% -> 50%) as experiment. running command: `redwoodctl route update --service inference-dedicated-us-east-1 --fallback eu-west --weight 10`

ops-runbook-bot: runbook step triggered: kvcache-check -> found elevated miss rate (90%) on shard 3. Suggest clearing prefix cache for hot models: `redwoodctl cache purge --shard 3 --prefix model/gptj-hot/`

jordan li: cache purge executed by alex. also rolled back last quantization kernel patch from yesterday on worker pool to rule out regression. command used: `kubectl patch ds inference-kernel -p '{"spec":{"template":{"metadata":{"annotations":{"rollout-revert":"2026-02-11"}}}}}'`

alex kim: patch applied. monitoring. error rate dropping but not done yet. live metrics: 5xx rate -> 7% (from 18%). p95 latency -> 1.2s down from 2.8s.

maya ramos: nice. i'm taking ownership at next status ping. alex — want to handoff so you can get rest? any customer comms started?

alex kim: handing off to @maya ramos for ongoing mitigation and post-incident follow-up. I'm going offline in ~25m. customer comms: CS has a draft for top impacted customers, will send update once we confirm stabilization.

maya ramos: taking ownership. plan: 1) maintain traffic split to eu-west while we complete health checks, 2) keep cache purge and reverted kernel, 3) run a controlled canary to bring traffic back to us-east, 4) prepare RCA notes and coordinate customer emails. I'll update here every 15m.

incident-bot: PD update: acknowledged by alex kim, ownership transferred to maya ramos (PD-assigned). escalation policy paused.

jordan li: small follow-up — scheduling a brief postmortem to capture runbook gaps: observed unclear guardrails around kvcache shard thresholds and no auto-purge. created task: ENG-5567.

sarah nguyen: CS note — two paying customers reported errors in the last 12m; outreach initiated. will wait for stabilization to update with ETA.

maya ramos: quick status after routing: 5xx -> 3.5%, p95 -> 800ms. rolling out 25% back to us-east as a canary. will pause if 5xx goes above 6%.

alex kim: :thumbsup: thanks team — leaving the bridge. maya, looping you into the PD incident and runbook edits.

maya ramos: signing off from bridge for now; i'll post final recap when PD is closed. assigning follow-ups: ENG-5567 (runbook), ENG-5568 (observability alert tuning), CS-321 (customer comms).

incident-bot: PD incident PDR-39284 marked as mitigated by maya ramos. please close PD once postmortem notes are attached.
